}\n  .foot-inner ul { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; }\n  .foot-inner li { padding: 0.15rem 0; }\n\n  /* Lightbox */\n  .lightbox {\n    position: fixed;\n    inset: 0;\n    background: rgba(20, 20, 20, 0.92);\n    display: none;\n    align-items: center;\n    justify-content: center;\n    padding: 2vh 2vw;\n    z-index: 100;\n  }\n  .lightbox.is-open { display: flex; }\n  .lightbox .lb-inner {\n    max-width: min(1400px, 96vw);\n    max-height: 96vh;\n    display: flex;\n    flex-direction: column;\n    align-items: center;\n  }\n  .lightbox img {\n    max-width: 100%;\n    max-height: 84vh;\n    height: auto;\n    width: auto;\n    background: #fff;\n    padding: 0.6rem;\n    border-radius: 2px;\n  }\n  .lightbox .lb-cap {\n    color: #e7e3da;\n    margin-top: 0.8rem;\n    font-size: 0.92rem;\n    max-width: 80ch;\n    text-align: center;\n    line-height: 1.5;\n  }\n  .lightbox .lb-close {\n    position: absolute;\n    top: 0.7rem;\n    right: 0.9rem;\n    background: transparent;\n    border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.4);\n    color: #f0ece3;\n    width: 2.4rem;\n    height: 2.4rem;\n    border-radius: 50%;\n    font-size: 1.1rem;\n    cursor: pointer;\n    line-height: 1;\n  }\n  .lightbox .lb-close:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.12); }\n  .lightbox .lb-close:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #fff; outline-offset: 2px; }\n\n  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {\n    * { transition: none !important; animation: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; }\n  }\n\n  /* Print: keep the page readable */\n  @media print {\n    nav.toc, .hero-actions, .lightbox { display: none !important; }\n    body { background: #fff; }\n    .card, .stat, figure { break-inside: avoid; }\n  }\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n\n<a class=\"skip\" href=\"#main\">Skip to main content</a>\n\n<header class=\"topbar\" role=\"banner\">\n  <div class=\"topbar-inner\">\n    <a class=\"brand\" href=\"#top\"><span class=\"brand-mark\">M-IRT</span>Reference-Free LLM Evaluation</a>\n    <nav class=\"toc\" aria-label=\"Page sections\">\n      <a href=\"#contributions\">Contributions</a>\n      <a href=\"#method\">Method</a>\n      <a href=\"#results\">Results</a>\n      <a href=\"#figures\">Figures</a>\n      <a href=\"#limitations\">Limitations</a>\n    </nav>\n  </div>\n</header>\n\n<main id=\"main\">\n\n  <section id=\"top\" aria-labelledby=\"paper-title\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Research paper</span>\n    <h1 id=\"paper-title\">M-IRT: Reference-Free LLM Evaluation via Samejima Graded Response Models on Dynamically Generated Metamorphic Item Clusters</h1>\n    <p class=\"byline\">Anonymous Authors</p>\n\n    <p class=\"lede\">\n      Static benchmarks with frozen answer keys are no longer trustworthy, since the\n      training corpora of modern language models have absorbed a large share of the\n      public web. This paper asks whether reasoning capability can be measured when\n      no answer key is trusted to be free of contamination, and answers yes: across\n      five public LLMs and one hundred dynamically generated\n      <em>Metamorphic Item Clusters</em>, the GRM-estimated latent ability &theta;\n      correlates with MMLU at <strong>Pearson&nbsp;r&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.975</strong>\n      (Spearman&nbsp;&rho;&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.90, Kendall&nbsp;&tau;&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.80),\n      with no fixed answer key in the loop. The full pipeline runs in three minutes\n      for under&nbsp;$0.05.\n    </p>\n\n    <div class=\"hero-actions\">\n      <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-0afdfa-checking-ai-logic-without-ground-truth@main/paper.pdf\"><span>Read the paper (PDF)</span><span class=\"arrow\" aria-hidden=\"true\">&rarr;</span></a>\n      <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-0afdfa-checking-ai-logic-without-ground-truth\"><span>Code &amp; data</span><span class=\"arrow\" aria-hidden=\"true\">&rarr;</span></a>\n    </div>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"contributions\" aria-labelledby=\"h-contrib\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Contributions</span>\n    <h2 id=\"h-contrib\">What this paper adds</h2>\n    <div class=\"cards\">\n      <article class=\"card\">\n        <span class=\"tag\">Framework</span>\n        <h3>Reference-free M-IRT</h3>\n        <p>A scoring framework that produces Metamorphic Item Clusters dynamically per session, derives ordinal coherence grades from relational invariants, and fits a Samejima Graded Response Model to recover a per-model latent ability &theta; with no fixed answer key in the loop.</p>\n      </article>\n      <article class=\"card\">\n        <span class=\"tag\">Pipeline</span>\n        <h3>Reproducible at $0.05</h3>\n        <p>One hundred MICs spanning propositional syllogisms and grade-school arithmetic, queried on five public LLMs, scored and fitted end-to-end in three minutes for under&nbsp;$0.05. The ablation against three binary consistency baselines on the same clusters shows &theta; (Pearson&nbsp;r&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.975) exceeds every one of them.</p>\n      </article>\n      <article class=\"card\">\n        <span class=\"tag\">Test &amp; protocol</span>\n        <h3>Stress test plus a clearly scoped next step</h3>\n        <p>An artificial stress test on Qwen&nbsp;2.5&nbsp;7B confirms coherence grading penalises internal inconsistency (&Delta;<sub>seed</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.07, &Delta;&theta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;\u22121.38). A natural-contamination protocol (system-prompt injection plus re-query) is laid out as the experiment the framework's hypothesis demands.</p>\n      </article>\n    </div>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"method\" aria-labelledby=\"h-method\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Method</span>\n    <h2 id=\"h-method\">How M-IRT scores a model without an answer key</h2>\n    <p>\n      Each cluster carries four variants &mdash; <em>seed</em>, <em>paraphrase</em>,\n      <em>negation</em>, and <em>inverse / contrapositive</em> &mdash; bound by a\n      relational invariant whose oracle is derivable from the question text alone.\n      No absolute label exists. A model is scored by how many of the four variants\n      it answers coherently; that count is mapped to a 3-point ordinal grade\n      (0&nbsp;=&nbsp;near-random, 1&nbsp;=&nbsp;partially coherent,\n      2&nbsp;=&nbsp;highly coherent) and a Samejima Graded Response Model\n      fits a per-model latent ability &theta; from the response matrix.\n    </p>\n\n    <figure>\n      <button class=\"thumb-btn\" data-figure=\"fig1\" aria-label=\"Open figure 1 in a lightbox\">\n        <span class=\"frame\"><img src=\"figures/fig1_v0.jpg\" alt=\"Four-stage M-IRT pipeline diagram: deterministic MIC generation, zero-shot model querying, ordinal coherence scoring, and Samejima GRM fitting with two validation sub-experiments.\" width=\"1024\" height=\"448\" loading=\"lazy\"></span>\n      </button>\n      <figcaption class=\"cap\"><strong>Figure 1.</strong> The four-stage M-IRT pipeline: deterministic MIC generation, zero-shot model querying, ordinal coherence scoring, and Samejima GRM fitting with two validation sub-experiments.</figcaption>\n    </figure>\n\n    <ol class=\"steps\" aria-label=\"Pipeline stages\">\n      <li>\n        <h3>Generate the clusters</h3>\n        <p>\n          Twelve logic templates and twelve arithmetic templates emit fifty\n          propositional-syllogism clusters and fifty grade-school word-problem\n          clusters, one hundred in total. Each cluster carries a relational\n          invariant table whose oracle is derivable from the question text\n          alone, so the contamination surface is the single session that\n          ran it.\n        </p>\n        <p>\n          Paraphrases use a noun pool disjoint from the seed so the seed and\n          the paraphrase never share vocabulary. The negation variant's\n          oracle is the Boolean complement (logic) or the fixed label\n          \"NO\" (arithmetic); the inverse variant's oracle is a quantity\n          that appears explicitly in the seed's question text.\n        </p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Query the models</h3>\n        <p>\n          Five public LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku 4.5, Llama 3.1 8B\n          Instruct, Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, Mistral Small 24B Instruct 2501)\n          receive each of the four hundred variant questions in a single\n          zero-shot prompt. All two thousand calls complete in 167&nbsp;s\n          at $0.048 cumulative spend, with the same prompt template\n          across models and no worked examples.\n        </p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Score ordinal coherence</h3>\n        <p>\n          For each (model, cluster) pair, count the variants whose response\n          matches the role-appropriate oracle and map that count to a\n          3-point ordinal grade. The scoring is deterministic and\n          parser-level, with no separate judge model or human rater.\n          Mapping the raw count 0&ndash;4 into three ordered bins is the\n          smallest K that separates \"near-random\" from \"partially\n          coherent\" from \"highly coherent\" and is the choice the present\n          panel of five models and one hundred items can stably fit.\n        </p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Fit a GRM and validate</h3>\n        <p>\n          Fit the Samejima Graded Response Model by marginal maximum\n          likelihood on the (5&nbsp;&times;&nbsp;100) response matrix, recovering\n          per-model &theta;, per-item discrimination &alpha;, and ordered\n          difficulty thresholds &beta;<sub>i,k</sub>. Two validation\n          sub-experiments check the result: an external correlation\n          against MMLU and HELM, and an artificial stress test that\n          forces internal inconsistency on thirty percent of clusters.\n        </p>\n      </li>\n    </ol>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"results\" aria-labelledby=\"h-results\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Results</span>\n    <h2 id=\"h-results\">What the five-model panel shows</h2>\n\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:1.2rem;\">Headline numbers</h3>\n    <div class=\"stats\">\n      <div class=\"stat\">\n        <div class=\"num\">0.975</div>\n        <div class=\"lbl\">Pearson correlation between &theta; and published MMLU accuracy across five public LLMs (95% bootstrap CI [0.59, 1.00]).</div>\n        <span class=\"src\">Table 1, Section 5.2</span>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"stat\">\n        <div class=\"num\">0.90 <span class=\"small\">/&nbsp;0.80</span></div>\n        <div class=\"lbl\">Spearman&nbsp;&rho; and Kendall&nbsp;&tau; of the &theta; ranking against MMLU. One rank inversion (Mistral Small 24B and Qwen 2.5 7B swapped) bounds the rank statistics at n&nbsp;=&nbsp;5.</div>\n        <span class=\"src\">Table 1, Section 5.2</span>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"stat\">\n        <div class=\"num\">$0.048</div>\n        <div class=\"lbl\">Cumulative spend across 2,000 model calls, 100 MICs, 5 models. Two thousand calls completed in 167&nbsp;s; total pipeline runtime 211&nbsp;s on a CPU-only container.</div>\n        <span class=\"src\">Section 4.2, Section 5.1</span>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:2.4rem;\">Latent ability ranking</h3>\n    <p>\n      Table&nbsp;1 sorts the five models by &theta;. The top two sit 0.13\n      &theta;-units apart; the bottom model is separated from the rest by\n      1.1&nbsp;&theta;-units. GRM-estimated &theta; versus published MMLU and HELM accuracy (n&nbsp;=&nbsp;5 models).</caption>\n        <thead>\n          <tr>\n            <th scope=\"col\">Model</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">&theta;</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">MMLU</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">HELM</th>\n          </tr>\n        </thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>openai/gpt-4o-mini</td><td>+3.69</td><td>0.820</td><td>0.79</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5</td><td>+3.56</td><td>0.801</td><td>0.78</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct</td><td>+0.07</td><td>0.707</td><td>0.69</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>mistralai/mistral-small-24b-instruct-2501</td><td>&minus;0.28</td><td>0.732</td><td>0.71</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct</td><td>&minus;1.37</td><td>0.684</td><td>0.65</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:2rem;\">Coherence distribution</h3>\n    <p>\n      The bottom-grade fraction separates the panel: Claude Haiku&nbsp;4.5\n      and GPT-4o-mini land at Y&nbsp;=&nbsp;0 on only five percent of\n      clusters; Llama&nbsp;3.1&nbsp;8B at twenty percent. }\n  }\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n\n<a class=\"skip\" href=\"#main\">Skip to main content</a>\n\n<header class=\"topbar\" role=\"banner\">\n  <div class=\"topbar-inner\">\n    <a class=\"brand\" href=\"#top\"><span class=\"brand-mark\">M-IRT</span>Reference-Free LLM Evaluation</a>\n    <nav class=\"toc\" aria-label=\"Page sections\">\n      <a href=\"#contributions\">Contributions</a>\n      <a href=\"#method\">Method</a>\n      <a href=\"#results\">Results</a>\n      <a href=\"#figures\">Figures</a>\n      <a href=\"#limitations\">Limitations</a>\n    </nav>\n  </div>\n</header>\n\n<main id=\"main\">\n\n  <section id=\"top\" aria-labelledby=\"paper-title\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Research paper</span>\n    <h1 id=\"paper-title\">M-IRT: Reference-Free LLM Evaluation via Samejima Graded Response Models on Dynamically Generated Metamorphic Item Clusters</h1>\n    <p class=\"byline\">Anonymous Authors</p>\n\n    <p class=\"lede\">\n      Static benchmarks with frozen answer keys are no longer trustworthy, since the\n      training corpora of modern language models have absorbed a large share of the\n      public web. This paper asks whether reasoning capability can be measured when\n      no answer key is trusted to be free of contamination, and answers yes: across\n      five public LLMs and one hundred dynamically generated\n      <em>Metamorphic Item Clusters</em>, the GRM-estimated latent ability &theta;\n      correlates with MMLU at <strong>Pearson&nbsp;r&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.975</strong>\n      (Spearman&nbsp;&rho;&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.90, Kendall&nbsp;&tau;&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.80),\n      with no fixed answer key in the loop. The full pipeline runs in three minutes\n      for under&nbsp;$0.05.\n    </p>\n\n    <div class=\"hero-actions\">\n      <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-0afdfa-checking-ai-logic-without-ground-truth@main/paper.pdf\"><span>Read the paper (PDF)</span><span class=\"arrow\" aria-hidden=\"true\">&rarr;</span></a>\n      <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-0afdfa-checking-ai-logic-without-ground-truth\"><span>Code &amp; data</span><span class=\"arrow\" aria-hidden=\"true\">&rarr;</span></a>\n    </div>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"contributions\" aria-labelledby=\"h-contrib\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Contributions</span>\n    <h2 id=\"h-contrib\">What this paper adds</h2>\n    <div class=\"cards\">\n      <article class=\"card\">\n        <span class=\"tag\">Framework</span>\n        <h3>Reference-free M-IRT</h3>\n        <p>A scoring framework that produces Metamorphic Item Clusters dynamically per session, derives ordinal coherence grades from relational invariants, and fits a Samejima Graded Response Model to recover a per-model latent ability &theta; with no fixed answer key in the loop.</p>\n      </article>\n      <article class=\"card\">\n        <span class=\"tag\">Pipeline</span>\n        <h3>Reproducible at $0.05</h3>\n        <p>One hundred MICs spanning propositional syllogisms and grade-school arithmetic, queried on five public LLMs, scored and fitted end-to-end in three minutes for under&nbsp;$0.05. The ablation against three binary consistency baselines on the same clusters shows &theta; (Pearson&nbsp;r&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.975) exceeds every one of them.</p>\n      </article>\n      <article class=\"card\">\n        <span class=\"tag\">Test &amp; protocol</span>\n        <h3>Stress test plus a clearly scoped next step</h3>\n        <p>An artificial stress test on Qwen&nbsp;2.5&nbsp;7B confirms coherence grading penalises internal inconsistency (&Delta;<sub>seed</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.07, &Delta;&theta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;\u22121.38). A natural-contamination protocol (system-prompt injection plus re-query) is laid out as the experiment the framework's hypothesis demands.</p>\n      </article>\n    </div>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"method\" aria-labelledby=\"h-method\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Method</span>\n    <h2 id=\"h-method\">How M-IRT scores a model without an answer key</h2>\n    <p>\n      Each cluster carries four variants &mdash; <em>seed</em>, <em>paraphrase</em>,\n      <em>negation</em>, and <em>inverse / contrapositive</em> &mdash; bound by a\n      relational invariant whose oracle is derivable from the question text alone.\n      No absolute label exists. A model is scored by how many of the four variants\n      it answers coherently; that count is mapped to a 3-point ordinal grade\n      (0&nbsp;=&nbsp;near-random, 1&nbsp;=&nbsp;partially coherent,\n      2&nbsp;=&nbsp;highly coherent) and a Samejima Graded Response Model\n      fits a per-model latent ability &theta; from the response matrix.\n    </p>\n\n    <figure>\n      <button class=\"thumb-btn\" data-figure=\"fig1\" aria-label=\"Open figure 1 in a lightbox\">\n        <span class=\"frame\"><img src=\"figures/fig1_v0.jpg\" alt=\"Four-stage M-IRT pipeline diagram: deterministic MIC generation, zero-shot model querying, ordinal coherence scoring, and Samejima GRM fitting with two validation sub-experiments.\" width=\"1024\" height=\"448\" loading=\"lazy\"></span>\n      </button>\n      <figcaption class=\"cap\"><strong>Figure 1.</strong> The four-stage M-IRT pipeline: deterministic MIC generation, zero-shot model querying, ordinal coherence scoring, and Samejima GRM fitting with two validation sub-experiments.</figcaption>\n    </figure>\n\n    <ol class=\"steps\" aria-label=\"Pipeline stages\">\n      <li>\n        <h3>Generate the clusters</h3>\n        <p>\n          Twelve logic templates and twelve arithmetic templates emit fifty\n          propositional-syllogism clusters and fifty grade-school word-problem\n          clusters, one hundred in total. Each cluster carries a relational\n          invariant table whose oracle is derivable from the question text\n          alone, so the contamination surface is the single session that\n          ran it.\n        </p>\n        <p>\n          Paraphrases use a noun pool disjoint from the seed so the seed and\n          the paraphrase never share vocabulary. The negation variant's\n          oracle is the Boolean complement (logic) or the fixed label\n          \"NO\" (arithmetic); the inverse variant's oracle is a quantity\n          that appears explicitly in the seed's question text.\n        </p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Query the models</h3>\n        <p>\n          Five public LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku 4.5, Llama 3.1 8B\n          Instruct, Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, Mistral Small 24B Instruct 2501)\n          receive each of the four hundred variant questions in a single\n          zero-shot prompt. All two thousand calls complete in 167&nbsp;s\n          at $0.048 cumulative spend, with the same prompt template\n          across models and no worked examples.\n        </p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Score ordinal coherence</h3>\n        <p>\n          For each (model, cluster) pair, count the variants whose response\n          matches the role-appropriate oracle and map that count to a\n          3-point ordinal grade. The scoring is deterministic and\n          parser-level, with no separate judge model or human rater.\n          Mapping the raw count 0&ndash;4 into three ordered bins is the\n          smallest K that separates \"near-random\" from \"partially\n          coherent\" from \"highly coherent\" and is the choice the present\n          panel of five models and one hundred items can stably fit.\n        </p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Fit a GRM and validate</h3>\n        <p>\n          Fit the Samejima Graded Response Model by marginal maximum\n          likelihood on the (5&nbsp;&times;&nbsp;100) response matrix, recovering\n          per-model &theta;, per-item discrimination &alpha;, and ordered\n          difficulty thresholds &beta;<sub>i,k</sub>. Two validation\n          sub-experiments check the result: an external correlation\n          against MMLU and HELM, and an artificial stress test that\n          forces internal inconsistency on thirty percent of clusters.\n        </p>\n      </li>\n    </ol>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"results\" aria-labelledby=\"h-results\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Results</span>\n    <h2 id=\"h-results\">What the five-model panel shows</h2>\n\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:1.2rem;\">Headline numbers</h3>\n    <div class=\"stats\">\n      <div class=\"stat\">\n        <div class=\"num\">0.975</div>\n        <div class=\"lbl\">Pearson correlation between &theta; and published MMLU accuracy across five public LLMs (95% bootstrap CI [0.59, 1.00]).</div>\n        <span class=\"src\">Table 1, Section 5.2</span>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"stat\">\n        <div class=\"num\">0.90 <span class=\"small\">/&nbsp;0.80</span></div>\n        <div class=\"lbl\">Spearman&nbsp;&rho; and Kendall&nbsp;&tau; of the &theta; ranking against MMLU. One rank inversion (Mistral Small 24B and Qwen 2.5 7B swapped) bounds the rank statistics at n&nbsp;=&nbsp;5.</div>\n        <span class=\"src\">Table 1, Section 5.2</span>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"stat\">\n        <div class=\"num\">$0.048</div>\n        <div class=\"lbl\">Cumulative spend across 2,000 model calls, 100 MICs, 5 models. Two thousand calls completed in 167&nbsp;s; total pipeline runtime 211&nbsp;s on a CPU-only container.</div>\n        <span class=\"src\">Section 4.2, Section 5.1</span>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:2.4rem;\">Latent ability ranking</h3>\n    <p>\n      Table&nbsp;1 sorts the five models by &theta;. The top two sit 0.13\n      &theta;-units apart; the bottom model is separated from the rest by\n      1.1&nbsp;&theta;-units. The &theta; ranking carries a single inversion\n      against MMLU (Mistral Small 24B and Qwen 2.5 7B swap), which is the\n      worst-case bound on the rank statistics at this sample size.\n    </p>\n\n    <div class=\"tablewrap\" role=\"region\" aria-label=\"Theta ranking table\">\n      <table>\n        <caption>Table 1. GRM-estimated &theta; versus published MMLU and HELM accuracy (n&nbsp;=&nbsp;5 models).</caption>\n        <thead>\n          <tr>\n            <th scope=\"col\">Model</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">&theta;</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">MMLU</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">HELM</th>\n          </tr>\n        </thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>openai/gpt-4o-mini</td><td>+3.69</td><td>0.820</td><td>0.79</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5</td><td>+3.56</td><td>0.801</td><td>0.78</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct</td><td>+0.07</td><td>0.707</td><td>0.69</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>mistralai/mistral-small-24b-instruct-2501</td><td>&minus;0.28</td><td>0.732</td><td>0.71</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct</td><td>&minus;1.37</td><td>0.684</td><td>0.65</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:2rem;\">Coherence distribution</h3>\n    <p>\n      The bottom-grade fraction separates the panel: Claude Haiku&nbsp;4.5\n      and GPT-4o-mini land at Y&nbsp;=&nbsp;0 on only five percent of\n      clusters; Llama&nbsp;3.1&nbsp;8B at twenty percent. The middle of\n      the table inverts against MMLU: Qwen's bottom-grade fraction\n      (16%) exceeds Mistral's (7%) despite Mistral's higher MMLU.\n    </p>\n\n    <div class=\"tablewrap\" role=\"region\" aria-label=\"Coherence distribution table\">\n      <table>\n        <caption>Table 2. Ordinal coherence distribution per model across 100 MICs.</caption>\n        <thead>\n          <tr>\n            <th scope=\"col\">Model</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">Y&nbsp;=&nbsp;0</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">Y&nbsp;=&nbsp;1</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">Y&nbsp;=&nbsp;2</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">mean raw correct</th>\n          </tr>\n        </thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5</td><td>5</td><td>21</td><td>74</td><td>3.21</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>openai/gpt-4o-mini</td><td>5</td><td>20</td><td>75</td><td>3.11</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>mistralai/mistral-small-24b-instruct-2501</td><td>7</td><td>19</td><td>74</td><td>2.94</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct</td><td>16</td><td>17</td><td>67</td><td>2.78</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct</td><td>20</td><td>26</td><td>54</td><td>2.32</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:2rem;\">Comparison against binary consistency baselines</h3>\n    <p>\n      The GRM &theta; outperforms three reference-free baselines on the\n      same clusters by Pearson&nbsp;r, while tying on Spearman&nbsp;&rho;\n      and Kendall&nbsp;&tau;. The four &theta; values for the four top\n      models (3.69, 3.56, 0.07, &minus;0.28) span 3.97 &theta;-units; the\n      binary metrics cluster between 0.83 and 0.95.\n    </p>\n\n    <div class=\"tablewrap\" role=\"region\" aria-label=\"Baseline correlation table\">\n      <table class=\"dense\">\n        <caption>Table 3. Reference-free metrics vs. MMLU and HELM accuracy on n&nbsp;=&nbsp;5 models.</caption>\n        <thead>\n          <tr>\n            <th scope=\"col\">Metric</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">r&nbsp;vs&nbsp;MMLU</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">&rho;&nbsp;vs&nbsp;MMLU</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">&tau;&nbsp;vs&nbsp;MMLU</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">r&nbsp;vs&nbsp;HELM</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">&rho;&nbsp;vs&nbsp;HELM</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">&tau;&nbsp;vs&nbsp;HELM</th>\n          </tr>\n        </thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>Seed-only accuracy</td><td>+0.900</td><td>+0.900</td><td>+0.800</td><td>+0.941</td><td>+0.900</td><td>+0.800</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Paraphrase agreement rate</td><td>+0.905</td><td>+0.900</td><td>+0.800</td><td>+0.943</td><td>+0.900</td><td>+0.800</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Negation invariance rate</td><td>+0.826</td><td>+0.800</td><td>+0.600</td><td>+0.886</td><td>+0.800</td><td>+0.600</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>Composite (mean of PA, NI)</td><td>+0.855</td><td>+0.900</td><td>+0.800</td><td>+0.909</td><td>+0.900</td><td>+0.800</td></tr>\n          <tr class=\"highlight\"><td>GRM &theta;</td><td>+0.975</td><td>+0.900</td><td>+0.800</td><td>+0.976</td><td>+0.900</td><td>+0.800</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:2rem;\">Stress test on Qwen 2.5 7B</h3>\n    <p>\n      On thirty percent of clusters the seed response is forced to the\n      oracle while the metamorphic variants stay untouched. Seed-only\n      accuracy rises by +0.07 on average; the GRM-estimated &theta; falls\n      by an average of &minus;1.382 with standard deviation 0.007 across\n      three random seeds. The sign flip on &theta; is the contamination-\n      resistance signal at the response-matrix level: forcing the seed\n      right while the metamorphic slots stay wrong produces a profile\n      the GRM penalises.\n    </p>\n\n    <div class=\"tablewrap\" role=\"region\" aria-label=\"Stress test table\">\n      <table>\n        <caption>Table 4. Stress test on Qwen 2.5 7B: seed response forced to oracle on 30% of clusters while metamorphic variants are unchanged.</caption>\n        <thead>\n          <tr>\n            <th scope=\"col\">Seed</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">Seed-only acc (clean)</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">Seed-only acc (stressed)</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">&Delta;&nbsp;seed-only</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">&theta; (clean)</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">&theta; (stressed)</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">&Delta;&theta;</th>\n          </tr>\n        </thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>0</td><td>0.78</td><td>0.85</td><td>+0.07</td><td>&minus;0.001</td><td>&minus;1.389</td><td>&minus;1.387</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>1</td><td>0.78</td><td>0.84</td><td>+0.06</td><td>&minus;0.001</td><td>&minus;1.387</td><td>&minus;1.385</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>42</td><td>0.78</td><td>0.86</td><td>+0.08</td><td>&minus;0.001</td><td>&minus;1.373</td><td>&minus;1.372</td></tr>\n          <tr class=\"highlight\"><td>mean</td><td>0.78</td><td>0.85</td><td>+0.07</td><td>&minus;0.001</td><td>&minus;1.382</td><td>&minus;1.382</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>std</td><td>&mdash;</td><td>&mdash;</td><td>0.01</td><td>&mdash;</td><td>&mdash;</td><td>0.007</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"figures\" aria-labelledby=\"h-figs\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Figures</span>\n    <h2 id=\"h-figs\">All four figures from the paper</h2>\n    <p style=\"color: var(--ink-2);\">Click any figure to enlarge. The lightbox closes on Escape, on the close button, or on a click outside the image.</p>\n\n    <div class=\"gallery\">\n      <figure>\n        <button class=\"thumb-btn\" data-figure=\"fig1\" aria-label=\"Open figure 1: M-IRT pipeline diagram, in a lightbox\">\n          <span class=\"frame\"><img src=\"figures/fig1_v0.jpg\" alt=\"M-IRT pipeline diagram showing four stages flowing left to right: deterministic MIC generation, zero-shot model querying of five LLMs, ordinal coherence scoring into a 5-by-100 response matrix, and Samejima GRM fitting with two validation sub-experiments.\" width=\"1024\" height=\"448\" loading=\"lazy\"></span>\n        </button>\n        <figcaption class=\"cap\"><strong>Figure 1.</strong> The four-stage M-IRT pipeline: deterministic MIC generation, zero-shot model querying, ordinal coherence scoring, and Samejima GRM fitting with two validation sub-experiments.</figcaption>\n      </figure>\n\n      <figure>\n        <button class=\"thumb-btn\" data-figure=\"fig2\" aria-label=\"Open figure 2: theta vs MMLU scatter, in a lightbox\">\n          <span class=\"frame\"><img src=\"figures/fig2_v0.png\" alt=\"Scatter plot of GRM-estimated theta (x-axis, range minus two to plus four) against MMLU accuracy (y-axis, range 0.60 to 0.85) for five LLMs. Five labelled points, two clustered at the upper right, one in the middle, and one at the lower left. Pearson r = 0.975 and Spearman rho = 0.90 are annotated.\" width=\"1200\" height=\"900\" loading=\"lazy\"></span>\n        </button>\n        <figcaption class=\"cap\"><strong>Figure 2.</strong> GRM-estimated &theta; versus published MMLU accuracy for n&nbsp;=&nbsp;5 LLMs. Pearson&nbsp;r&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.975, Spearman&nbsp;&rho;&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.90, Kendall&nbsp;&tau;&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.80. The single rank inversion (Mistral Small 24B and Qwen 2.5 7B are swapped) bounds the rank statistics at this sample size.</figcaption>\n      </figure>\n\n      <figure>\n        <button class=\"thumb-btn\" data-figure=\"fig3\" aria-label=\"Open figure 3: per-model coherence distribution, in a lightbox\">\n          <span class=\"frame\"><img src=\"figures/fig3_v0.png\" alt=\"Horizontal stacked bar chart showing the ordinal coherence distribution for five models across 100 MICs. Each bar segments into Y equals 0 in red (near-random, five to twenty percent), Y equals 1 in yellow (partially coherent, seventeen to twenty-six percent), and Y equals 2 in green (highly coherent, fifty-four to seventy-five percent).\" width=\"1400\" height=\"788\" loading=\"lazy\"></span>\n        </button>\n        <figcaption class=\"cap\"><strong>Figure 3.</strong> Ordinal coherence distribution per model across 100 MICs. The top two models achieve the top grade on 74&ndash;75% of clusters and the bottom grade on only 5%. Llama 3.1 8B sits at the floor on 20% of clusters, a 4&times; spread that the GRM exploits.</figcaption>\n      </figure>\n\n      <figure>\n        <button class=\"thumb-btn\" data-figure=\"fig4\" aria-label=\"Open figure 4: stress test of coherence scoring, in a lightbox\">\n          <span class=\"frame\"><img src=\"figures/fig4_v0.png\" alt=\"Two-panel bar chart of the stress test on Qwen 2.5 7B. Left panel shows seed-only accuracy for three random seeds: clean at 0.78 across all, stressed at 0.85, 0.84, and 0.86, with an annotation of plus 0.07. Right panel shows theta: clean at minus 0.001 across all, stressed at minus 1.389, minus 1.387, and minus 1.373, with an annotation of minus 1.382 mean and 0.007 standard deviation.\" width=\"1826\" height=\"1267\" loading=\"lazy\"></span>\n        </button>\n        <figcaption class=\"cap\"><strong>Figure 4.</strong> Stress test on Qwen 2.5 7B: seed-only accuracy rises by +0.07 on average under artificial internal-inconsistency, while the GRM-estimated &theta; drops by &minus;1.382 across three random seeds with standard deviation 0.007. The sign flip on &theta; is the contamination-resistance signal at the response-matrix level.</figcaption>\n      </figure>\n    </div>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"limitations\" class=\"limits\" aria-labelledby=\"h-limits\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Limitations</span>\n    <h2 id=\"h-limits\">Where the present evidence falls short</h2>\n    <ul>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Five-model panel</h3>\n        <p>The bootstrap CI on Pearson&nbsp;r spans [0.59, 1.00]; the lower bound already allows r&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.59, well below the r&nbsp;&gt;&nbsp;0.85 hypothesis criterion. The hypothesis specifies n&nbsp;&ge;&nbsp;15; the present artifact runs at n&nbsp;=&nbsp;5 because the OpenRouter cost ceiling restricted the panel.</p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Two reasoning domains</h3>\n        <p>MICs cover propositional syllogisms and grade-school arithmetic. Real reasoning also includes multi-hop reading comprehension and first-order logic (FOLIO). The reported MMLU correlation therefore reflects the syllogistic-plus-arithmetic component of reasoning capability, not MMLU's history, law, medicine, or biology domains directly.</p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Artificial stress test, not natural contamination</h3>\n        <p>The response-matrix-level stress test confirms that coherence grading penalises an internally inconsistent profile, but does not test the contamination-resistance claim in the realistic sense. A natural-contamination experiment (inject the seed oracle into the system prompt, re-query all four variants, measure whether coherence rises on the metamorphic slots) is the proper test and is listed as future work.</p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Twelve templates per domain</h3>\n        <p>Twelve logic templates and twelve arithmetic templates cover the classical syllogistic forms and the most common word-problem operations, but are not exhaustive. A larger generator bank would yield finer per-item discrimination estimates.</p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Polytomous response scale</h3>\n        <p>The 0/1/2 mapping compresses 5 raw counts (0&ndash;4) into 3 categories. With a larger panel, K&nbsp;=&nbsp;4 or K&nbsp;=&nbsp;5 would let the GRM exploit more granularity at the cost of greater estimation variance.</p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Reference-free for what?</h3>\n        <p>A model that memorises the form of the metamorphic relation (e.g., that \"not P\" flips a V/I label) would still answer all four variants coherently and would receive a high &theta;. That is the correct outcome (the model has internalised a logical rule) but it is not a contamination-resistance result. The natural-contamination protocol is the test that distinguishes \"internalised the rule\" from \"memorised the seeds\".</p>\n      </li>\n    </ul>\n  </section>\n\n</main>\n\n<footer role=\"contentinfo\">\n  <div class=\"foot-inner\">\n    <div>\n      <h4>About this page</h4>\n      <p>A presentation page for the paper <em>M-IRT: Reference-Free LLM Evaluation via Samejima Graded Response Models on Dynamically Generated Metamorphic Item Clusters</em>. Anonymous Authors. All numbers and claims come from the paper itself.</p>\n    </div>\n    <div>\n      <h4>Links</h4>\n      <ul>\n        <li><a href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-0afdfa-checking-ai-logic-without-ground-truth@main/paper.pdf\">Paper PDF</a></li>\n        <li><a href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-0afdfa-checking-ai-logic-without-ground-truth\">Code repository</a></li>\n      </ul>\n    </div>\n    <div>\n      <h4>Citation</h4>\n      <p style=\"font-family: ui-monospace, 'SFMono-Regular', Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.82rem; color: var(--ink-3); margin: 0;\">Anonymous Authors. M-IRT: Reference-Free LLM Evaluation via Samejima Graded Response Models on Dynamically Generated Metamorphic Item Clusters. 2025.</p>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n</footer>\n\n<div class=\"lightbox\" id=\"lightbox\" role=\"dialog\" aria-modal=\"true\" aria-label=\"Figure viewer\" tabindex=\"-1\">\n  <button class=\"lb-close\" type=\"button\" aria-label=\"Close figure viewer\" data-close>&times;</button>\n  <div class=\"lb-inner\">\n    <p class=\"lb-cap\" id=\"lb-cap\"></p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n\n<script>\n(function () {\n  // Lightbox\n  var lb = document.getElementById('lightbox');\n  var lbCap = document.getElementById('lb-cap');\n  var lbInner = lb.querySelector('.lb-inner');\n  var lbImg = null;\n  var lastTrigger = null;\n\n  function openLb(trigger) {\n    var fig = trigger.closest('figure');\n    if (!fig) return;\n    var img = fig.querySelector('img');\n    var cap = fig.querySelector('figcaption');\n    if (!img) return;\n    // Create a fresh <img> inside the lightbox so the only image tags in\n    // the static HTML are the four figure thumbnails. The lightbox image\n    // is built on demand, with a src that resolves to the same file.\n    lbImg = document.createElement('img');\n    lbImg.alt = img.alt;\n    lbImg.src = img.getAttribute('src');\n    lbInner.insertBefore(lbImg, lbCap);\n    lbCap.innerHTML = cap ? cap.innerHTML : '';\n    lb.classList.add('is-open');\n    lb.removeAttribute('hidden');\n    lastTrigger = trigger;\n    document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden';\n    // Move focus to the close button so screen readers announce the dialog\n    var btn = lb.querySelector('.lb-close');\n    if (btn) btn.focus();\n  }\n\n  function closeLb() {\n    if (!lb.classList.contains('is-open')) return;\n    lb.classList.remove('is-open');\n    document.body.style.overflow = '';\n    if (lastTrigger && typeof lastTrigger.focus === 'function') {\n      lastTrigger.focus();\n    }\n  }\n\n  document.querySelectorAll('.thumb-btn').forEach(function (btn) {\n    btn.addEventListener('click', function () { openLb(btn); });\n  });\n\n  lb.addEventListener('click', function (e) {\n    if (e.target === lb || e.target.hasAttribute('data-close')) {\n      closeLb();\n    }\n  });\n\n  document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {\n    if (e.key === 'Escape' && lb.classList.contains('is-open')) {\n      closeLb();\n    }\n  });\n\n  // Focus trap while the lightbox is open\n  lb.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {\n    if (e.key !== 'Tab' || !lb.classList.contains('is-open')) return;\n    var focusables = lb.querySelectorAll('button, [href], [tabindex]:not([tabindex=\"-1\"])');\n    if (focusables.length === 0) return;\n    var first = focusables[0];\n    var last = focusables[focusables.length - 1];\n    if (e.shiftKey && document.activeElement === first) {\n      e.preventDefault();\n      last.focus();\n    } else if (!e.shiftKey && document.activeElement === last) {\n      e.preventDefault();\n      first.focus();\n    }\n  });\n\n  // Sticky nav: highlight current section\n  var tocLinks = document.querySelectorAll('nav.toc a');\n  var sections = [];\n  tocLinks.forEach(function (link) {\n    var id = link.getAttribute('href').replace('#', '');\n    var sec = document.getElementById(id);\n    if (sec) sections.push({ id: id, el: sec, link: link });\n  });\n\n  function onScroll() {\n    var y = window.scrollY + 120;\n    var current = sections[0] ? sections[0].id : null;\n    for (var i = 0; i < sections.length; i++) {\n      if (sections[i].el.offsetTop <= y) current = sections[i].id;\n    }\n    tocLinks.forEach(function (l) { l.classList.remove('is-active'); });\n    if (current) {\n      var match = document.querySelector('nav.toc a[href=\"#' + current + '\"]');\n      if (match) match.classList.add('is-active');\n    }\n  }\n  window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, { passive: true });\n  onScroll();\n})();\n</script>\n\n</body>\n</html>\n", "new_content": "<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html lang=\"en\">\n<head>\n<meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n<meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n<title>M-IRT: Reference-Free LLM Evaluation via Samejima Graded Response Models on Dynamically Generated Metamorphic Item Clusters</title>\n<meta name=\"description\" content=\"A reference-free LLM evaluation framework: dynamically generated Metamorphic Item Clusters scored by a Samejima Graded Response Model, correlating with MMLU at Pearson r = 0.975 on five public LLMs.\">\n<style>\n  :root {\n    --bg: #fbfaf8;\n    --surface: #ffffff;\n    --ink: #1a1a1a;\n    --ink-2: #4a4a4a;\n    --ink-3: #6e6e6e;\n    --rule: #e6e2da;\n    --rule-strong: #c9c4b8;\n    --accent: #8a2a2a;\n    --accent-soft: #f4e8e8;\n    --code-bg: #f3efe6;\n    --measure: 68ch;\n    --gutter: 1.5rem;\n  }\n  * { box-sizing: border-box; }\n  html { -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; text-size-adjust: 100%; }\n  body {\n    margin: 0;\n    background: var(--bg);\n    color: var(--ink);\n    font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, \"Segoe UI\", \"Helvetica Neue\", Arial, sans-serif;\n    font-size: 17px;\n    line-height: 1.62;\n    font-feature-settings: \"kern\" 1, \"liga\" 1, \"calt\" 1;\n    -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;\n    -moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale;\n  }\n  a {\n    color: var(--accent);\n    text-decoration: underline;\n    text-underline-offset: 2px;\n    text-decoration-thickness: 1px;\n  }\n  a:hover { text-decoration-thickness: 2px; }\n  a:focus-visible {\n    outline: 2px solid var(--accent);\n    outline-offset: 3px;\n    border-radius: 2px;\n  }\n  .skip {\n    position: absolute;\n    left: -9999px;\n    top: 0;\n    background: var(--ink);\n    color: var(--bg);\n    padding: 0.6rem 1rem;\n    z-index: 1000;\n  }\n  .skip:focus { left: 0.5rem; top: 0.5rem; }\n\n  /* Top bar with byline + nav */\n  .topbar {\n    border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);\n    background: var(--bg);\n  }\n  .topbar-inner {\n    max-width: 1180px;\n    margin: 0 auto;\n    padding: 0.9rem var(--gutter);\n    display: flex;\n    flex-wrap: wrap;\n    align-items: center;\n    gap: 0.5rem 1.4rem;\n  }\n  .brand {\n    font-weight: 600;\n    letter-spacing: -0.01em;\n    color: var(--ink);\n    text-decoration: none;\n  }\n  .brand .brand-mark {\n    display: inline-block;\n    padding: 0.05em 0.4em;\n    background: var(--ink);\n    color: var(--bg);\n    border-radius: 3px;\n    margin-right: 0.45em;\n    font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;\n  }\n  nav.toc {\n    margin-left: auto;\n    display: flex;\n    flex-wrap: wrap;\n    gap: 0.25rem 1.1rem;\n    font-size: 14px;\n  }\n  nav.toc a {\n    color: var(--ink-2);\n    text-decoration: none;\n    padding: 0.15rem 0;\n    border-bottom: 1px solid transparent;\n  }\n  nav.toc a:hover { color: var(--ink); }\n  .thumb-btn {\n    display: block;\n    width: 100%;\n    background: transparent;\n    border: 0;\n    padding: 0;\n    cursor: zoom-in;\n    text-align: left;\n  }\n  .thumb-btn:focus-visible {\n    outline: 2px solid var(--accent);\n    outline-offset: -2px;\n  }\n  .zoomhint {\n    display: inline-block;\n    margin-top: 0.4rem;\n    font-size: 0.78rem;\n    color: var(--ink-3);\n  }\n\n  /* Limitations */\n  .limits ul {\n    list-style: none;\n    padding: 0;\n    margin: 0;\n  }\n  .limits li {\n    border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);\n    padding: 1rem 0 1rem 1.8rem;\n    position: relative;\n  }\n  .limits li:first-child { border-top: 0; }\n  .foot-inner ul { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; }\n  .foot-inner li { padding: 0.15rem 0; }\n\n  /* Lightbox */\n  .lightbox {\n    position: fixed;\n    inset: 0;\n    background: rgba(20, 20, 20, 0.92);\n    display: none;\n    align-items: center;\n    justify-content: center;\n    padding: 2vh 2vw;\n    z-index: 100;\n  }\n  .lightbox.is-open { display: flex; }\n  .lightbox .lb-close:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #fff; outline-offset: 2px; }\n\n  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {\n    * { transition: none !important; animation: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; }\n  }\n\n  /* Print: keep the page readable */\n  @media print {\n    nav.toc, .hero-actions, .lightbox { display: none !important; }\n    body { background: #fff; }\n    .card, .stat, figure { break-inside: avoid; }\n  }\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n\n<a class=\"skip\" href=\"#main\">Skip to main content</a>\n\n<header class=\"topbar\" role=\"banner\">\n  <div class=\"topbar-inner\">\n    <a class=\"brand\" href=\"#top\"><span class=\"brand-mark\">M-IRT</span>Reference-Free LLM Evaluation</a>\n    <nav class=\"toc\" aria-label=\"Page sections\">\n      <a href=\"#contributions\">Contributions</a>\n      <a href=\"#method\">Method</a>\n      <a href=\"#results\">Results</a>\n      <a href=\"#figures\">Figures</a>\n      <a href=\"#limitations\">Limitations</a>\n    </nav>\n  </div>\n</header>\n\n<main id=\"main\">\n\n  <section id=\"top\" aria-labelledby=\"paper-title\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Research paper</span>\n    <h1 id=\"paper-title\">M-IRT: Reference-Free LLM Evaluation via Samejima Graded Response Models on Dynamically Generated Metamorphic Item Clusters</h1>\n    <p class=\"byline\">Anonymous Authors</p>\n\n    <p class=\"lede\">\n      Static benchmarks with frozen answer keys are no longer trustworthy, since the\n      training corpora of modern language models have absorbed a large share of the\n      public web. This paper asks whether reasoning capability can be measured when\n      no answer key is trusted to be free of contamination, and answers yes: across\n      five public LLMs and one hundred dynamically generated\n      <em>Metamorphic Item Clusters</em>, the GRM-estimated latent ability &theta;\n      correlates with MMLU at <strong>Pearson&nbsp;r&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.975</strong>\n      (Spearman&nbsp;&rho;&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.90, Kendall&nbsp;&tau;&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.80),\n      with no fixed answer key in the loop. The full pipeline runs in three minutes\n      for under&nbsp;$0.05.\n    </p>\n\n    <div class=\"hero-actions\">\n      <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-0afdfa-checking-ai-logic-without-ground-truth@main/paper.pdf\"><span>Read the paper (PDF)</span><span class=\"arrow\" aria-hidden=\"true\">&rarr;</span></a>\n      <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-0afdfa-checking-ai-logic-without-ground-truth\"><span>Code &amp; data</span><span class=\"arrow\" aria-hidden=\"true\">&rarr;</span></a>\n    </div>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"contributions\" aria-labelledby=\"h-contrib\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Contributions</span>\n    <h2 id=\"h-contrib\">What this paper adds</h2>\n    <div class=\"cards\">\n      <article class=\"card\">\n        <span class=\"tag\">Framework</span>\n        <h3>Reference-free M-IRT</h3>\n        <p>A scoring framework that produces Metamorphic Item Clusters dynamically per session, derives ordinal coherence grades from relational invariants, and fits a Samejima Graded Response Model to recover a per-model latent ability &theta; with no fixed answer key in the loop.</p>\n      </article>\n      <article class=\"card\">\n        <span class=\"tag\">Pipeline</span>\n        <h3>Reproducible at $0.05</h3>\n        <p>One hundred MICs spanning propositional syllogisms and grade-school arithmetic, queried on five public LLMs, scored and fitted end-to-end in three minutes for under&nbsp;$0.05. The ablation against three binary consistency baselines on the same clusters shows &theta; (Pearson&nbsp;r&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.975) exceeds every one of them.</p>\n      </article>\n      <article class=\"card\">\n        <span class=\"tag\">Test &amp; protocol</span>\n        <h3>Stress test plus a clearly scoped next step</h3>\n        <p>An artificial stress test on Qwen&nbsp;2.5&nbsp;7B confirms coherence grading penalises internal inconsistency (&Delta;<sub>seed</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;+0.07, &Delta;&theta;&nbsp;=&nbsp;\u22121.38). A natural-contamination protocol (system-prompt injection plus re-query) is laid out as the experiment the framework's hypothesis demands.</p>\n      </article>\n    </div>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"method\" aria-labelledby=\"h-method\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Method</span>\n    <h2 id=\"h-method\">How M-IRT scores a model without an answer key</h2>\n    <p>\n      Each cluster carries four variants &mdash; <em>seed</em>, <em>paraphrase</em>,\n      <em>negation</em>, and <em>inverse / contrapositive</em> &mdash; bound by a\n      relational invariant whose oracle is derivable from the question text alone.\n      No absolute label exists. A model is scored by how many of the four variants\n      it answers coherently; that count is mapped to a 3-point ordinal grade\n      (0&nbsp;=&nbsp;near-random, 1&nbsp;=&nbsp;partially coherent,\n      2&nbsp;=&nbsp;highly coherent) and a Samejima Graded Response Model\n      fits a per-model latent ability &theta; from the response matrix.\n    </p>\n\n    <figure>\n      <button class=\"thumb-btn\" data-figure=\"fig1\" aria-label=\"Open figure 1 in a lightbox\">\n        <span class=\"frame\"><img src=\"figures/fig1_v0.jpg\" alt=\"Four-stage M-IRT pipeline diagram: deterministic MIC generation, zero-shot model querying, ordinal coherence scoring, and Samejima GRM fitting with two validation sub-experiments.\" width=\"1024\" height=\"448\" loading=\"lazy\"></span>\n      </button>\n      <figcaption class=\"cap\"><strong>Figure 1.</strong> The four-stage M-IRT pipeline: deterministic MIC generation, zero-shot model querying, ordinal coherence scoring, and Samejima GRM fitting with two validation sub-experiments.</figcaption>\n    </figure>\n\n    <ol class=\"steps\" aria-label=\"Pipeline stages\">\n      <li>\n        <h3>Generate the clusters</h3>\n        <p>\n          Twelve logic templates and twelve arithmetic templates emit fifty\n          propositional-syllogism clusters and fifty grade-school word-problem\n          clusters, one hundred in total. Each cluster carries a relational\n          invariant table whose oracle is derivable from the question text\n          alone, so the contamination surface is the single session that\n          ran it.\n        </p>\n        <p>\n          Paraphrases use a noun pool disjoint from the seed so the seed and\n          the paraphrase never share vocabulary. The negation variant's\n          oracle is the Boolean complement (logic) or the fixed label\n          \"NO\" (arithmetic); the inverse variant's oracle is a quantity\n          that appears explicitly in the seed's question text.\n        </p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Query the models</h3>\n        <p>\n          Five public LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Claude Haiku 4.5, Llama 3.1 8B\n          Instruct, Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, Mistral Small 24B Instruct 2501)\n          receive each of the four hundred variant questions in a single\n          zero-shot prompt. All two thousand calls complete in 167&nbsp;s\n          at $0.048 cumulative spend, with the same prompt template\n          across models and no worked examples.\n        </p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Score ordinal coherence</h3>\n        <p>\n          For each (model, cluster) pair, count the variants whose response\n          matches the role-appropriate oracle and map that count to a\n          3-point ordinal grade. The scoring is deterministic and\n          parser-level, with no separate judge model or human rater.\n          Mapping the raw count 0&ndash;4 into three ordered bins is the\n          smallest K that separates \"near-random\" from \"partially\n          coherent\" from \"highly coherent\" and is the choice the present\n          panel of five models and one hundred items can stably fit.\n        </p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Fit a GRM and validate</h3>\n        <p>\n          Fit the Samejima Graded Response Model by marginal maximum\n          likelihood on the (5&nbsp;&times;&nbsp;100) response matrix, recovering\n          per-model &theta;, per-item discrimination &alpha;, and ordered\n          difficulty thresholds &beta;<sub>i,k</sub>. Two validation\n          sub-experiments check the result: an external correlation\n          against MMLU and HELM, and an artificial stress test that\n          forces internal inconsistency on thirty percent of clusters.\n        </p>\n      </li>\n    </ol>\n  </section>\n\n  <section id=\"results\" aria-labelledby=\"h-results\">\n    <span class=\"eyebrow\">Results</span>\n    <h2 id=\"h-results\">What the five-model panel shows</h2>\n\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:1.2rem;\">Headline numbers</h3>\n    <div class=\"stats\">\n      <div class=\"stat\">\n        <div class=\"num\">0.975</div>\n        <div class=\"lbl\">Pearson correlation between &theta; and published MMLU accuracy across five public LLMs (95% bootstrap CI [0.59, 1.00]).</div>\n        <span class=\"src\">Table 1, Section 5.2</span>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"stat\">\n        <div class=\"num\">0.90 <span class=\"small\">/&nbsp;0.80</span></div>\n        <div class=\"lbl\">Spearman&nbsp;&rho; and Kendall&nbsp;&tau; of the &theta; ranking against MMLU. One rank inversion (Mistral Small 24B and Qwen 2.5 7B swapped) bounds the rank statistics at n&nbsp;=&nbsp;5.</div>\n        <span class=\"src\">Table 1, Section 5.2</span>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"stat\">\n        <div class=\"num\">$0.048</div>\n        <div class=\"lbl\">Cumulative spend across 2,000 model calls, 100 MICs, 5 models. Two thousand calls completed in 167&nbsp;s; total pipeline runtime 211&nbsp;s on a CPU-only container.</div>\n        <span class=\"src\">Section 4.2, Section 5.1</span>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:2.4rem;\">Latent ability ranking</h3>\n    <p>\n      Table&nbsp;1 sorts the five models by &theta;. The top two sit 0.13\n      &theta;-units apart; the bottom model is separated from the rest by\n      1.1&nbsp;&theta;-units. The &theta; ranking carries a single inversion\n      against MMLU (Mistral Small 24B and Qwen 2.5 7B swap), which is the\n      worst-case bound on the rank statistics at this sample size.\n    </p>\n\n    <div class=\"tablewrap\" role=\"region\" aria-label=\"Theta ranking table\">\n      <table>\n        <caption>Table 1. GRM-estimated &theta; versus published MMLU and HELM accuracy (n&nbsp;=&nbsp;5 models).</caption>\n        <thead>\n          <tr>\n            <th scope=\"col\">Model</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">&theta;</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">MMLU</th>\n            <th scope=\"col\">HELM</th>\n          </tr>\n        </thead>\n        <tbody>\n          <tr><td>openai/gpt-4o-mini</td><td>+3.69</td><td>0.820</td><td>0.79</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5</td><td>+3.56</td><td>0.801</td><td>0.78</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct</td><td>+0.07</td><td>0.707</td><td>0.69</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>mistralai/mistral-small-24b-instruct-2501</td><td>&minus;0.28</td><td>0.732</td><td>0.71</td></tr>\n          <tr><td>meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct</td><td>&minus;1.37</td><td>0.684</td><td>0.65</td></tr>\n        </tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>\n\n    <h3 style=\"margin-top:2rem;\">Coherence distribution</h3>\n    <p>\n      The bottom-grade fraction separates the panel: Claude Haiku&nbsp;4.5\n      and GPT-4o-mini land at Y&nbsp;=&nbsp;0 on only five percent of\n      clusters; Llama&nbsp;3.1&nbsp;8B at twenty percent. The middle of\n      the table inverts against MMLU: Qwen's bottom-grade fraction\n      (16%) exceeds Mistral's (7%) despite Mistral's higher MMLU.\n    </p>\n\n    <div class=\"tablewrap\" role=\"region\" aria-label=\"Coherence distribution table\">\n      <table>\n        <caption>Table 2. Real reasoning also includes multi-hop reading comprehension and first-order logic (FOLIO). The reported MMLU correlation therefore reflects the syllogistic-plus-arithmetic component of reasoning capability, not MMLU's history, law, medicine, or biology domains directly.</p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Artificial stress test, not natural contamination</h3>\n        <p>The response-matrix-level stress test confirms that coherence grading penalises an internally inconsistent profile, but does not test the contamination-resistance claim in the realistic sense. A natural-contamination experiment (inject the seed oracle into the system prompt, re-query all four variants, measure whether coherence rises on the metamorphic slots) is the proper test and is listed as future work.</p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Twelve templates per domain</h3>\n        <p>Twelve logic templates and twelve arithmetic templates cover the classical syllogistic forms and the most common word-problem operations, but are not exhaustive. With a larger panel, K&nbsp;=&nbsp;4 or K&nbsp;=&nbsp;5 would let the GRM exploit more granularity at the cost of greater estimation variance.</p>\n      </li>\n      <li>\n        <h3>Reference-free for what?</h3>\n        <p>A model that memorises the form of the metamorphic relation (e.g., that \"not P\" flips a V/I label) would still answer all four variants coherently and would receive a high &theta;. That is the correct outcome (the model has internalised a logical rule) but it is not a contamination-resistance result.
